t:
(a) Public Law 89–188, as amended, is amended under the heading “Inside the United States” in section 101, as follows:

        (1) 
Under the heading “continental army command (Second Army)” with respect to Fort Lee, Virginia, strike out “$700,000” and insert in place thereof “$925,000”.
 
        (2) 
Under the subheading “continental army command, less Army Materiel Command (Fifth Army)” with respect to Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri, strike out “$16,084,000” and insert in place thereof “$16,536,000”.
  
    (b) 
Public Law 89–188 is amended by striking out in clause (1) of section 602 “$253,722,000” and “$310,583,000” and inserting “$254,399,000” and “$311,260,000”, respectively.

fable.w: This section only amends dollar amounts in a prior military construction authorization act for Fort Lee and Fort Leonard Wood. There is no tempting reading here: no outside party is consulted, no hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is created. It is purely a funding-figure amendment that stays entirely within the federal government.
fable.s: strike out “$700,000” and insert in place thereof “$925,000”

qwen_block.w: This section amends a previous law to adjust specific dollar amounts for military construction projects. It involves no consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. The text is purely administrative and financial, dealing with internal government appropriations.
qwen_block.s: strike out “$700,000” and insert in place thereof “$925,000”

opus.w: The section only replaces authorized dollar amounts for military construction at Fort Lee and Fort Leonard Wood and in the section 602 totals. No outside party (state, tribe, public, expert or company) is consulted or given any part in a federal decision. It does not require rulemaking or grant anyone a right to sue. Calling this participation would mean treating a routine funding amendment as a procedural mechanism, which it isn't.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** This section only changes dollar figures in Public Law 89–188, a military construction authorization: amounts for Fort Lee, for Fort Leonard Wood, and the totals in section 602. The words "continental army command" or "amended" might look procedural, but nothing here involves anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends specific dollar amounts in an existing appropriations law. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities. The changes are legislative adjustments to funding levels, not participatory mechanisms.
qwen_chat.s: Under the heading “continental army command (Second Army)” with respect to Fort Lee, Virginia, strike out “$700,000” and insert in place thereof “$925,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing appropriation amounts implies a decision-making process involving stakeholders, but the text itself only lists numerical changes to statutory funding levels. There is no mention of consultation, hearings, advisory boards, or public comment periods. The actors involved are implicitly Congress (amending the law) and the executive branch (receiving funds), all of whom are inside the federal government.
